content:
ashley: FYI — Velociti is seeing repeated 429s on their Dedicated pool during a marketing blast. Customer reports time window 2024-06-12 18:10–18:25 UTC, lots of short streaming calls. They say tokens/sec SLO got violated and requests started getting rejected by admission controller. Escalating.

ashley: summary: ~25% of requests returned 429 admission_rejected, errors spike started at 18:12. Provisioned TPS ~200, observed burst ~1.1k for ~3m. Burst credits reported as exhausted in logs. Account: velociti-prod-007, pool: ded-pool-3a

mike_oncall: ack — putting oncall badge. Can you paste one or two request IDs and the admission controller log lines? Also need the dedicated pool id (did you mean pool:ded-pool-3a?)

ashley: yes pool is ded-pool-3a. sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d. admission log snippet:

```
[2024-06-12T18:12:07Z] admission_controller: admit=false account=velociti-prod-007 pool=ded-pool-3a reason=burst_credits_exhausted headroom_ms=0 tokens_required=264 burst_credits_remaining=0 req_id=req_0a1b2c3d
[2024-06-12T18:12:11Z] admission_controller: admit=false account=velociti-prod-007 pool=ded-pool-3a reason=admission_queue_full queue_len=120 req_id=req_0a1b2c3e
```

ashley: metric snapshot around 18:12 (from internal dashboards): total_tokens_sec=1120, provisioned_tps=200, avg_latency_ms=320, streaming_conns=480

leo_runtime: looking. Two quick asks: 1) did autoscaler start any new nodes during that spike? 2) any node-level pod evictions or OOMs? If autoscaler didn't start because of placement constraints it explains the backlog.

sara_support: checked billing/auth path — account is active and not suspended. No billing blocks. The burst-credit ledger shows a sudden decline consistent with many short stream sessions (streaming keeps KV cache warm and consumes extra tokens per connection).

jared_sre: grabbing admission-controller logs and k8s events now. Quick grep I ran shows multiple admission-controller WARNs right before rejects:

```
WARN admission: headroom < min_headroom_threshold for account=velociti-prod-007 pool=ded-pool-3a
ERROR autoscaler: scale_request_rejected reason=pod_anti_affinity_conflict zone=us-west-2a
```

jared_sre: also seeing HPA didn't trigger because the pending pods failed nodeSelector matching (we had a recent affinity policy change in ded-pool-3a). Filing a short blameless note about that.

mike_oncall: can you paste the reproduce curl so we can validate with a small synthetic test? Need to confirm whether it's tokens/sec or concurrency causing bank to drain.

ashley: reproduce steps I used with the customer's payload (redacted):

```
# simulate 400 concurrent streaming clients for 180s
for i in {1..400}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
    -d '{"model":"rwl-1.0","stream":true,"prompt":"short prompt"}' &
done
```

ashley: when run from a perf worker we immediately saturated tokens/sec and saw admissions flip to reject after ~45s. Logs align with burst credits dropping to 0.

leo_runtime: concrete mitigation steps:
- temporary: reduce concurrency from 400 -> 80 on customer side, advise backoff/retry 503->linear
- quick infra: force-scale the pool to +3 pods (manual override) while we fix anti-affinity rule

leo_runtime: CLI to force scale (internal):

```
# internal command to raise pool replica target
redwoodctl pools set-replicas --pool ded-pool-3a --replicas 12 --reason "emergency-scale velociti"
```

mike_oncall: i'm going to apply the temporary scale and also add a small burst-topup to the account so they don't see further rejects while we resolve placement. @sara_support can you confirm topup command and cost owner ok?

sara_support: confirmed — we can credit 60s worth of burst headroom for the account (manual grant). Cost owner approved. Command:

```
supportctl grant-burst --account velociti-prod-007 --seconds 60 --note "emergency 2024-06-12"
```

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2024-1798 — severity: high — owners: @mike_oncall, @leo_runtime, @sara_support

mike_oncall: scale applied and burst granted. Monitoring now.

jared_sre: after scale, queue_len dropped from 120 -> 8, admission logs show admits resuming. I still see a gap: autoscaler rejected due to anti-affinity; that was the root cause. We will rollback the affinity PR in staging and fast-track the fix to prod for ded-pool-3a.

ashley: customer confirmed reduced errors after your actions. They ran another blast and saw <1% 429s. They accepted temporary throttling guidance.

leo_runtime: follow-up action items:
- fix anti-affinity rule and deploy
- add an alert: autoscaler_reject_count > 3 in 5m => page oncall
- add a dashboard tile showing burst_credits_remaining per account (alert on <30s)

ashley: thanks everyone — posting the trace link for reference: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/velociti/req_0a1b2c3d

mike_oncall: closing incident when postmortem notes uploaded. Moving to postmortems channel after this thread.

ashley: will prepare a short summary and customer-facing update. Thanks :thumbsup:
